moat_against: Commodity price-taker: earnings are set by the LME aluminum price and alumina index, not by Alcoa
ROE swung from -15.3% (2023) to +18.9% (2025) in fundamentals.json — no through-cycle return above the cost of capital
Energy is ~30% of smelting cost and largely bought at market; tariff exposure on Canadian metal
Alumina in surplus near $350-370/t into 2026-27 and Chinese supply caps the upside
South32 upstream deal adds debt ($2.6B notes issued) and ~17M new shares before synergies are proven
moat_for: Vertically integrated bauxite → alumina → aluminum chain; full control of AWAC since the Aug 2024 Alumina Ltd deal
Scale: one of the world's largest bauxite and alumina producers, with long-life Western Australian bauxite
Low-carbon product line (EcoLum / ELYSIS development) positioned for CBAM-style premiums
Smelter portfolio restarted toward structurally short North American / European markets
moat_justification: Weak moat 3/10: a vertically integrated, scaled upstream producer, but a pure commodity price-taker. fundamentals.json carries no roic_proxy or gross-margin series (operating income / COGS are not tagged in the companyfacts extraction, both print null for every year), and the ROE series that is printed swings from -15.3% in 2023 to +18.9% in 2025 — returns are the aluminum price, not a franchise. No written reason can put a 7+ moat on that history.
name: Alcoa Corp
one_liner: Cyclical commodity price-taker, moat 3/10 — on the current TTM base it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 5.25%, weighted IV@15% $9.11 vs $41.45 price); it would need a price near $9.11 to clear the 15% hurdle on these cash flows.
